title: Modulatory Effects of Alpha-Mangostin Mediated by SIRT1/3-FOXO3a Pathway in Oxidative Stress-Induced Neuronal Cells.
authors: Ruankham, Waralee; Suwanjang, Wilasinee; Phopin, Kamonrat; Songtawee, Napat; Prachayasittikul, Virapong; Prachayasittikul, Supaluk
one_liner_zh: 该文研究α-倒捻子素通过SIRT1/3-FOXO3a通路保护神经元免受氧化应激，仅含分子对接预测小分子与SIRT1结合，无蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: alpha-Mangostin, a polyphenolic xanthone, is primarily found in the pericarp of mangosteen throughout Southeast Asia and is considered as the "Queen of Fruit" in Thailand. Nonetheless, it is not clarified how alpha-mangostin protects neuronal cells against oxidative stress. OBJECTIVE: In this study, molecular mechanisms underlying the neuroprotective effect of alpha-mangostin in defending hydrogen peroxide (H(2)O(2))-induced neurotoxicity was explored. METHODS: cytotoxicity, reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, apoptotic cascades, and protein expression profiles were performed incorporation of molecular docking. RESULTS: Human SH-SY5Y cells were pretreated with 1 muM alpha-mangostin for 3 h prior to exposure to 400 muM H(2)O(2). alpha-Mangostin significantly inhibited oxidative stress-induced cell death in neuronal cells by reducing BAX protein, decreasing caspase-3/7 activation, and increasing anti-apoptotic BCL-2 protein. Collectively, alpha-mangostin was demonstrated to be a prominent ROS suppressor which reversed the reduction of antioxidant enzymes (CAT and SOD2). Surprisingly, alpha-mangostin significantly promoted the expression of the sirtuin family and the FOXO3a transcription factor exerting beneficial effects on cell survival and longevity. A molecular docking study predicted that alpha-mangostin is directly bound to the active site of SIRT1. CONCLUSION: Findings from this study suggest that alpha-mangostin potentially serves as a promising therapeutic compound against oxidative stress by activation of the SIRT1/3-FOXO3a pathway comparable to the effect of memantine, an anti-AD drug used for the treatment of moderate to severe dementia.
abstract_zh: 背景：α-倒捻子素（alpha-Mangostin）是一种多酚类氧杂蒽酮，主要分布于东南亚山竹果皮中，在泰国被誉为“水果皇后”。然而，α-倒捻子素如何保护神经细胞免受氧化应激的影响尚未明确。目的：本研究探讨了α-倒捻子素在防御过氧化氢（H(2)O(2)）诱导的神经毒性中的神经保护作用的分子机制。方法：进行了细胞毒性、活性氧（ROS）生成、凋亡级联反应及蛋白表达谱分析，并结合分子对接技术。结果：人SH-SY5Y细胞在暴露于400 μM H(2)O(2)前，先用1 μM α-倒捻子素预处理3小时。α-倒捻子素通过降低BAX蛋白、减少caspase-3/7活化及增加抗凋亡BCL-2蛋白，显著抑制了氧化应激诱导的神经细胞死亡。总体而言，α-倒捻子素被证明是一种显著的ROS抑制剂，可逆转抗氧化酶（CAT和SOD2）的减少。令人惊讶的是，α-倒捻子素显著促进了sirtuin家族及FOXO3a转录因子的表达，对细胞存活和寿命产生有益影响。分子对接研究预测，α-倒捻子素直接结合于SIRT1的活性位点。结论：本研究结果表明，α-倒捻子素通过激活SIRT1/3-FOXO3a通路，可能作为一种有前景的治疗氧化应激的化合物，其效果与美金刚（memantine，一种用于治疗中重度痴呆的抗阿尔茨海默病药物）相当。
